policy: Resolve public game identities first, then use physical figure names, set names, and resolved component inventories as separate evidence. Negative accessory states may be confirmed from explicit component absence/presence within an otherwise identity-matched physical candidate, but do not imply exact artwork equivalence.

records.reason: Hermit is an explicit Skywalker Saga Lando identity, while Unmasked is a source-local state selector. The 2019 old-Lando Episode IX release is the appropriate physical age/timeline family, but the catalog does not independently identify the Hermit/Unmasked game state; exact equivalence remains visual pending.

Scavenger Grey Vest is an explicit game appearance and is the more descriptive form of the previously reviewed Rey_Vest asset. The 2015 Episode VII Rey family is relevant, but physical catalog terminology does not independently encode the grey-vest state; preserve the game appearance while exact equivalence remains visual pending.

The game explicitly distinguishes FN-2187 - No Helmet. The physical sw0716 identity independently matches FN-2187, and the repo's resolved component inventory for the corresponding physical candidate contains Finn hair rather than a stormtrooper helmet. This verifies the identity plus negative helmet state; exact digital texture reuse remains visual pending.

Heavy Assault is an explicit Skywalker Saga B1 Battle Droid role. None of the currently supported physical candidate names or component summaries independently identify Heavy Assault; Kashyyyk, Geonosian, Rocket and generic bent-arm battle droids are different variants. Preserve the game role rather than choosing the highest same-family score.

Pilot - Helmet is an explicit Skywalker Saga Padmé variant, but the current crosswalk has no Padmé physical candidate satisfying both character identity and pilot/helmet state. The top lexical hits are unrelated pilots, so no physical identity should be inferred.

systemic_findings: Set names can carry variant identifiers absent from Rebrickable figure names (for example set 30605 identifies FN-2187).
Resolved component inventories can validate negative accessory states such as NoHelmet when the candidate identity is independently established.
Game role variants such as Heavy Assault must not collapse onto nearby physical family members without role-specific evidence.
